value.body: A field investigator collects first-hand data for research and evaluation studies by visiting households, villages or institutions and conducting structured interviews. Employers include survey and research agencies, NGOs, university research projects and development consultancies. A typical day involves travel to the study area, interviewing respondents in the local language and uploading data each evening.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: Any BA; social science graduates preferred

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Tablet-based survey apps, paper schedules, GPS

items.label: Households interviewed in NFHS-5
items.note: One national survey round; data collected by field teams across all districts
items.source: NFHS-5 National Report, IIPS / Ministry of Health & Family Welfare

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Research agencies and NGOs hire field investigators for each study, usually after a short training on the questionnaire. Fluency in the local language of the study area is often the deciding factor. Good field records can lead to supervisor and research-associate roles.

value.title: At a glance
items: Much of the work is contract-based for the length of a study.
Anthropology training in observation and fieldwork transfers directly.
Next roles: field supervisor, research associate, project coordinator.
